passages.s: Thaw, and resolue it selfe into a Dew: Or that the Euerlasting had not fixt His Cannon 'gainst Selfe-slaughter.
Tender your selfe more dearly; Or not to crack the winde of the poore Phrase, Roaming it thus, you'l tender me a foole Ophe.
At closes in the consequence: At friend, or so, and Gentleman Polon.

Slanders Sir: for the Satyricall slaue saies here, that old men haue gray Beards; that their faces are wrinkled; their eyes purging thicke Amber, or Plum-Tree Gumme: and that they haue a plentifull locke of Wit, together with weake Hammes.

So after Pyrrhus pause, A rowsed Vengeance sets him new a-worke, And neuer did the Cyclops hammers fall On Mars his Armours, forg'd for proofe Eterne, With lesse remorse then Pyrrhus bleeding sword Now falles on Priam.
Or if thou wilt needs Marry, marry a fool: for Wise men know well enough, what monsters you make of them.
The instances that second Marriage moue, Are base respects of Thrift, but none of Loue.
My Lord, he's going to his Mothers Closset: Behinde the Arras Ile conuey my selfe To heare the Processe.
Come sir, to draw toward an end with you.
Conscience and Grace, to the profoundest Pit.

Why I will fight with him vppon this Theme.

When I burnt in desire to question them further, they made themselues Ayre, into which they vanish'd.
Will it not be receiu'd, When we haue mark'd with blood those sleepie two Of his owne Chamber, and vs'd their very Daggers, That they haue don't?
My Hands are of your colour: but I shame To weare a Heart so white.
This murtherous Shaft that's shot, Hath not yet lighted: and our safest way, Is to auoid the ayme.

Of sorryest Fancies your Companions making, Vsing those Thoughts, which should indeed haue dy'd With them they thinke on: things without all remedie Should be without regard: what's done, is done Macb.

Adde thereto a Tigers Chawdron, For th' Ingredience of our Cawdron All.

All these are portable, With other Graces weigh'd Mal.
I haue too Nights watch'd with you, but can perceiue no truth in your report.
Therein the Patient Must minister to himselfe Macb.
Or else misgraffed, in respect of yeares Her.
Some of your French Crownes haue no haire at all, and then you will play bare-fac'd.
What worser place can I beg in your loue, (And yet a place of high respect with me) Then to be vsed as you doe your dogge Dem.
Lysander on the ground; Deade or asleepe?

Most radiant Piramus, most Lilly white of hue, Of colour like the red rose on triumphant bryer, Most brisky Iuuenall, and eke most louely Iew, As true as truest horse, that yet would neuer tyre, Ile meete thee Piramus, at Ninnies toombe Pet.
Ah good Demetrius, wilt thou giue him me?
Lysanders loue (that would not let him bide) Faire Helena; who more engilds the night, Then all yon fierie oes, and eies of light.
Why will you suffer her to flout me thus?
Truly a pecke of Prouender; I could munch your good dry Oates.
And for the morning now is something worne, Our purpos'd hunting shall be set aside.
That is some Satire keene and criticall, Not sorting with a nuptiall ceremonie Lis.
I kisse the wals hole, not your lips at all Pir.
Iudge me the world, if 'tis not grosse in sense, That thou hast practis'd on her with foule Charmes, Abus'd her delicate Youth, with Drugs or Minerals, That weakens Motion.
So that (deere Lords) if I be left behind A Moth of Peace, and he go to the Warre, The Rites for why I loue him, are bereft me: And I a heauie interim shall support By his deere absence.
I am about it, but indeed my inuention comes from my pate, as Birdlyme do's from Freeze, it pluckes out Braines and all.
To morrow with your earliest, Let me haue speech with you.
Looke if my gentle Loue be not rais'd vp: Ile make thee an example Des.
Assure thee, If I do vow a friendship, Ile performe it To the last Article.
Ile haue the worke tane out, And giu't Iago: what he will do with it Heauen knowes, not I: I nothing, but to please his Fantasie.
Why do you speake so startingly, and rash?
This is the Monkeys owne giuing out: She is perswaded I will marry her Out of her owne loue & flattery, not out of my promise Oth.
But alas, to make me The fixed Figure for the time of Scorne, To point his slow, and mouing finger at.
That Song to night, Will not go from my mind: I haue much to do, But to go hang my head all at one side And sing it like poore Barbarie: prythee dispatch Aemi.
Alacke, my Lord, What may you meane by that?
To give away yourself, keeps yourself still, And you must live, drawn by your own sweet skill.
Yet him for this my love no whit disdaineth; Suns of the world may stain when heaven’s sun staineth.
XLIV If the dull substance of my flesh were thought, Injurious distance should not stop my way; For then despite of space I would be brought, From limits far remote, where thou dost stay.
I have no precious time at all to spend; Nor services to do, till you require.
LXX That thou art blam’d shall not be thy defect, For slander’s mark was ever yet the fair; The ornament of beauty is suspect, A crow that flies in heaven’s sweetest air.
LXXX O how I faint when I of you do write, Knowing a better spirit doth use your name, And in the praise thereof spends all his might, To make me tongue-tied speaking of your fame!
Such is my love, to thee I so belong, That for thy right, myself will bear all wrong.
What old December’s bareness everywhere!

So all their praises are but prophecies Of this our time, all you prefiguring; And for they looked but with divining eyes, They had not skill enough your worth to sing: For we, which now behold these present days, Have eyes to wonder, but lack tongues to praise.

Thus policy in love, to anticipate The ills that were not, grew to faults assur’d, And brought to medicine a healthful state Which, rank of goodness, would by ill be cur’d; But thence I learn and find the lesson true, Drugs poison him that so fell sick of you.
Since saucy jacks so happy are in this, Give them thy fingers, me thy lips to kiss.
CXXXVIII When my love swears that she is made of truth, I do believe her though I know she lies, That she might think me some untutor’d youth, Unlearned in the world’s false subtleties.
